# alpinejs-router

> alpinejs-router (npm: `@shaun/alpinejs-router`) is a lightweight client-side router plugin for Alpine.js 3. Routes are declared in HTML: each route is a `<template x-route="/path">`, links are `<a x-link href="/path">`, and route state is read through the `$router` magic.

It supports dynamic params (`/users/:id`, exposed as `$router.params.id`), custom regex params (`/:orderId(\d+)`), a not-found template (`x-route.notfound`), external route templates fetched on demand or preloaded (`template="/user.html"`, `template.preload`), and hash or HTML5 history modes with an optional base path (`$router.config({ mode: 'hash', base: '/app' })`). The minified CDN build is about 3.2 kB gzipped and has no dependencies besides Alpine.js. MIT licensed.

It does not provide navigation guards, routes defined in JavaScript, or server-side rendering. In HTML5 (`web`) mode the server must serve `index.html` for unknown paths.

Quick start (CDN; load the router before Alpine):

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@shaun/alpinejs-router@1.x.x/dist/cdn.min.js" defer></script>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/alpinejs@3.x.x/dist/cdn.min.js" defer></script>

<body x-data>
  <a x-link href="/hello/alpine">Hello</a>
  <template x-route="/hello/:name">
    <main>Hello <span x-text="$router.params.name"></span></main>
  </template>
  <template x-route.notfound><main>Not found</main></template>
</body>
```

With a bundler:

```js
import Alpine from 'alpinejs'
import router from '@shaun/alpinejs-router'

Alpine.plugin(router)
Alpine.start()
```
